Flake-boundary clarification: `flake-detection` and `flake-release` implement section 11.5's test quarantine ledger; they never invent a SHA-held set. Detection is called only after one named check test fails and then passes on the bare same-workspace/no-code-change re-run. Given `test_id`, the signature-deduped report `signature`, and the resulting Suggestion Box `box_id`, it appends one `signal` event keyed `flake/<box_id>` with body `{kind: flake_detected, test_id, signature, box_id}` and folds that test into quarantine. Detection itself is dormant construction through a `compose_daemon_flake`-style hook in `squatch/daemon.py`; no production composition in `squatch/__main__.py` or `squatch/drain.py` calls or constructs it yet, though `squatch.flake` may be import-reachable through daemon composition.

Mechanical release is identity-bound to the SAME ledger entry: the box resolution status for `box_id` must name `fix_stem`, that exact stem must have merged, and the named test's green rerun must be observed. It appends one `signal` event keyed `flake-release/<box_id>/<fix_stem>` with body `{kind: flake_released, test_id, signature, box_id, fix_stem}` BEFORE folding the entry out of quarantine. A second release of the same identity appends no event and changes no state. The direct release-hook proof lives in fenced `tests/test_flake.py`; existing production composition tests remain unchanged preservation suites unless a later activation actually calls the hook. Manual `resume` remains the separate operator override from section 11.5.

Storm-boundary clarification: `storm-ledger` implements only section 12's dormant occurrence window. A caller supplies the already-normalized failure `signature`, a durable producer-supplied `occurrence_id` that is unique per arrival and stable on replay, and the optional `emitting_stage` (`None` for a non-pipeline producer). Recording appends one `signal` keyed `storm-occurrence/<signature>/<occurrence_id>` with body `{kind: storm_occurrence, signature, occurrence_id, emitting_stage}`; an existing identical key is an idempotent no-event. The fold reads the complete ordered journal stream across active and immutable rolled segments, groups by signature, and at an injected `now` retains envelope timestamps in the half-open window `(now - T, now]`. Its observable result is the ordered live occurrence identities, count, and whether `count > K`, with shipped constants `K=5` and `T=1 hour`; an occurrence exactly on the lower boundary is expired. It emits no trip signal, box message, notification, or dispatch hold. `tests/test_storm.py` directly proves duplicate replay, the exact event key/body, strict threshold and boundary behavior, and a window spanning a rolled-segment boundary. Dormancy is an AST transitive `squatch.*` import-closure proof rooted at `squatch/__main__.py`: `squatch.storm` is not production-reachable before the later wiring admission.

The later storm admissions consume that one ledger contract without redefining it. `storm-producer-wiring` treats the then-existing `squatch/storm.py` and `tests/test_storm.py` as Context and wires every box arrival, including a signature-dedup hit, to one stable occurrence identity through the daemon/box seam while leaving production composition dormant. `storm-notification-activation` fences the real production root `squatch/__main__.py` in addition to storm/box/daemon and their tests, replaces the dormancy assertion, and activates the section 12 trip signal plus its one P0 `failure_report`; the trip identity is deterministic over `(signature, first_live_occurrence_id, crossing_occurrence_id)`, so replay cannot mint a second trip for the same crossing. Its fence also includes `tests/test_drain.py` to migrate only `test_bootstrap_drain_never_scans_or_mutates_the_box`'s obsolete blanket assertion that no journal event contains `box`: the test must continue to prove the drain neither mutates nor triages the pending Box record, while allowing the composed lock holder's required `storm_occurrence` reconciliation events. Because embedding that large predecessor suite would breach `REQ_RENDER_HEADROOM`, `tests/test_drain.py` is a fenced on-demand inspection exception, not embedded Context. Dispatch suppression remains OUT until the separate KNOWN-DEEP `storm-dispatch-hold` admission. For the continuation that authors those two seeds, only `tests/test_storm_producer.py`, `tests/test_storm_notification_activation.py`, and its next numbered seeded test are sibling-new paths; the already-merged storm module and test are not sibling-new.

Storm-dispatch-hold ownership clarification: the exact KNOWN-DEEP `storm-dispatch-hold` fence is `squatch/storm.py`, `squatch/control.py`, `squatch/daemon.py`, `squatch/drain.py`, `squatch/__main__.py`, new `tests/test_storm_hold.py`, and every then-existing storm predecessor test whose dispatch-absence assertion it migrates (`tests/test_storm.py`, `tests/test_storm_producer.py`, and `tests/test_storm_notification_activation.py` where that assertion is present). This supersedes the compact-registry shorthand above. A bootstrap drain offer is a whole ticket, not a selectable pipeline stage, so `emitting_stage` remains diagnostic and MUST NOT be used as the dispatch selector. This admission extends occurrence and trip bodies with `emitting_origin`, always present in newly written events as a string or `null` and validated with the same nullable-string rule as `emitting_stage`; `StormLedger.record` accepts it as an optional argument defaulting to `None`, and replay treats legacy occurrence/trip events that omit it as `None`. The producer supplies the Box message's origin. The live drain holds only the ticket whose `stem == emitting_origin`, before retry draws or any other durable dispatch accounting. Other ticket stems remain eligible, and a null or non-ticket origin creates no global hold. Trip identity and occurrence identity remain unchanged and replay-stable. The predecessor storm tests may migrate exact occurrence/trip body, key-set, and `_event` fixture assertions only to add and validate this field; their identity, trip-id, report, and all other positive assertions remain unchanged. The CLI composition root binds the journal-derived per-stem hold and identity-bound `resume` path into the live drain. `tests/test_daemon_composition.py` is read-only preservation Context. Because embedding both production roots with the storm module, control/daemon seams, predecessor tests, and preservation harness exceeds `REQ_RENDER_HEADROOM`, `squatch/drain.py` and `squatch/__main__.py` are fenced on-demand inspection exceptions rather than embedded Context; every other existing fence path is embedded Context. The seed test pins that exact fence and partition, authoring-time sizes, high/high tier, predecessor migration/preservation classification, and a max-effort render within headroom. No later admission activates this hold: this ticket is its production owner before `phase3-exit`.

Checkpoint-push ownership clarification: the exact `checkpoint-push` fence is new `squatch/checkpoint.py`, `squatch/daemon.py`, `squatch/git.py`, new `tests/test_checkpoint.py`, and `tests/test_git.py`. The Git seam owns a public argv-only push operation and its direct test; checkpoint composition calls only that seam and re-fires an incomplete push after restart without duplicating a completed one. Its exact embedded Context is `squatch/daemon.py`, `squatch/git.py`, and `tests/test_git.py`; the two new paths are sibling-new. The following `phase3-continue-19` seed's exact Context is `tests/test_seeded_phase3_11.py` as the established continuation pattern plus `tests/test_daemon_composition.py` as production-composition evidence. These exact partitions are pinned by `tests/test_seeded_phase3_18.py` and supersede the compact-registry shorthand.
